title: Enhancing Skills and Capabilities of Nurses and Nursing Aides
what_it_is: Enhancing Skills and Capabilities of Nurses and Nursing Aides

sections.label: Aging population and healthcare needs
sections.summary: An aging population will increase and complicate healthcare needs, and the speaker agrees ENs and care staff should be upskilled to perform wider patient care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As our population ages, healthcare needs will increase and become more complex.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We agree with the Member that we should continue to upskill ENs and support care staff to perform a wider scope of patient care.

sections.label: ENs upgrading to registered nurses
sections.summary: A 2014 National Nursing Taskforce recommendation lets ENs with three years' experience and an employer's testimonial take bridging and nursing diploma courses, with MOH funding; diploma enrolment rose 7% from 237 in 2014 to 253 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As part of the recommendations by the National Nursing Taskforce in 2014, more ENs can progress to become RNs by undertaking the Certificate in Bridging Studies for ENs course and, subsequently, the Diploma in Nursing course, if they have at least three years of post-enrolment work experience and an employer's testimonial.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has also increased funding for our public healthcare institutions to support the upgrading of ENs to RNs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With these changes, the number of ENs enrolling in the Diploma in Nursing course increased by 7% from 237 in 2014, to 253 in 2016.

sections.label: Nursing aides and subcutaneous injections
sections.summary: Nursing aides cannot administer insulin and other subcutaneous injections to nursing home residents; trained nurses, RNs and ENs do so because insulin is a high-alert medication.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Nursing aides are currently not allowed to administer insulin and other subcutaneous injections to nursing home residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Such injections are to be done by nurses, RNs and ENs, with training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This is in view that insulin is classed under the group of high-alert medications, which are medications that are most likely to cause significant harm to the patient, even when used as intended.

sections.label: Reviewing injections by nursing aides
sections.summary: MOH will work with nursing homes to review whether nursing aides and other support care staff may, with appropriate training, administer subcutaneous injections while maintaining safe care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Nonetheless, as I have noted earlier in my reply, we are looking at the expanding role and scope of patient care by upskilling our ENs and support care staff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, MOH will work with the nursing homes to review whether nursing aides and other support care staff may be allowed, with appropriate training, to administer subcutaneous injections, while maintaining safe care.

sections.label: Committee reviewing nursing curriculum
sections.summary: A committee is reviewing the curriculum and training of nurses to expand their role and scope.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I am speaking on this, there is a committee that is looking at reviewing the curriculum and training of nurses, to expand their role and scope.
